order.subject: math
order.requests: AP style: shared data sets, a segmented bar graph, an estimate-r question and a multi-part written answer. Every student gets her own numbers.

notes: Show your work on number answers

documents.title: Two-Variable Data Quiz
documents.directions: Answer every question. Some questions share a data set: it is shown with each of them. Calculators are allowed.

q1.prompt: What percent of the grade 9 students in the survey walk to school?
q1.why: Walk among grade 9 only: 7 ÷ 48 = 14.6%. The other choices divide by everyone (78), by all walkers (17), or count the car riders.

q2.prompt: Of all the students in the survey who walk to school, what percent are in grade 12? Round to one decimal place.

q3.prompt: Is there an association between grade and how students get to school in this survey? Answer in two parts.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Give the percent of grade 9 students and the percent of grade 12 students who ride the bus.
parts.answer: 29.2% of grade 9 (14 of 48) and 13.3% of grade 12 (4 of 30).
checklist: Each percent is out of its own grade's total, not out of everyone

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Do these data show an association? Explain, using the graph or the percents.
parts.answer: Yes. The percent who ride the bus is different in the two grades (29.2% and 13.3%), and the bars are divided differently, so knowing a student's grade changes how likely each way to school is.
checklist: Says yes, there is an association
Compares the same way to school across the two grades, using percents (the bars), not counts
Answers in context: grade and way to school

q3.why: An association means the conditional percents differ between groups: the bars of a segmented bar graph are not split the same way.

q4.prompt: Which value is closest to the correlation r for these data?
q4.why: The dots lie close to a line, so the association is fairly strong; the sign of r is the direction of the trend. r is about -0.75.

q6.prompt: The least-squares line $\hat{y} = 27.1 + 0.7x$ was fit to some data. One data point is (11, 36). Find the residual of this point.
